text:
noah: Hey team, first morning! M2 MacBook, zsh. Ran the repo dotfiles installer but my shell still picks /usr/bin/node. asdf plugins show nodejs 18.16.0 installed. Shims are in ~/.asdf/shims. Any zsh-specific magic to ensure shims are used? Also what's the recommended local place for REDWOOD_API_KEY for quick experiments?
rameen: welcome noah! Short checklist: 1) Put PATH modifications in ~/.zprofile (login shells) not ~/.zshrc. Prepend asdf shims: `export PATH=\"$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH\"`. 2) Add `eval \"$(asdf init zsh)\"`. 3) run `asdf reshim nodejs`.
kai: also confirm `brew --prefix` returns /opt/homebrew on M1/M2. If you have Intel brew (/usr/local) you might hit binary mismatch when compiling gems or native modules.
noah: moved the init to ~/.zprofile and ran reshim; `node --version` now shows v18 as expected, thanks. About REDWOOD_API_KEY — should I stash it in .envrc, .local.env, or 1Password?
infra: we keep secrets in 1Password. For local dev we prefer direnv: add `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` to a repo .envrc and `direnv allow`. Don't commit keys. If you need a personal dev key, open a request in #support and we'll create a short-lived test key.
noah: ran into GPG pinentry errors when importing commit key (error mentions pinentry-curses). Any fast mac fix?
rameen: `brew install pinentry-mac` then in `~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf` set `pinentry-program /opt/homebrew/bin/pinentry-mac` and add `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` to ~/.zprofile. Restart agent: `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent && gpgconf --launch gpg-agent`.
kai: quick additional note: for ruby builds with asdf/ruby set openssl flags if using brew openssl: `export LDFLAGS=\"-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib\"` and `export CPPFLAGS=\"-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include\"` before `asdf install ruby <ver>`.
noah: got gpg and node sorted. One minor thing: the dotfiles installer added an ssh config that points to the mac keychain, but ssh-add isn't remembering the key after reboot. Any mac sidebar?
rameen: run `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` and add that command to your login script. Also ensure `UseKeychain yes` and `AddKeysToAgent yes` in ~/.ssh/config. There's a helper `dotfiles/scripts/ssh-load.sh` that keeps it friendly.
devex-bot: (bot) Hi noah — if you'd like a 30m pairing session for setup, reply "pair" and I'll DM you available slots. Onboarding checklist: https://handbook.redwood.dev/onboarding/dev-setup
noah: appreciate this, everything mostly green. I'll open a support ticket for a dev API key. Thanks all :thumbsup:
